scenario.title: Explore Repair
scenario.premise: They explore whether repair is possible while explicitly keeping the outcome undecided.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Before we decide whether to end this, I want to ask if repair feels possible to you.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I do not know yet, but I am willing to look at what would need to change.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: For me, repair would need consistent follow through, not only good intentions.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That is fair. I need to consider whether I can offer that consistently.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We are exploring repair without promising that the relationship will continue.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I understand. Can we talk honestly about whether this relationship can continue?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, I know the question is serious, and I do not want to avoid it.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I am not asking for an immediate decision in the first minute.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Thank you. I need enough space to explain what has brought me here.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would you like to speak first while I listen?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes. I have felt increasingly alone when our conflicts stay unresolved.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Which unresolved conflict has affected you most?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: The repeated cancellations without notice have made reliability hard to trust.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I hear that the pattern matters more than one cancelled plan.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Exactly. One change is manageable, but repetition has changed how I feel.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Do you believe the trust can be repaired?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I do not know yet, and that uncertainty is why we need this conversation.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I can accept that you do not have an answer yet.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I appreciate that. I want us to examine the reality before choosing an ending.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What would reliability need to look like for you now?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Clear notice, fewer promises, and follow-through on the plans we do make.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I have promised more than my capacity allowed.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: That honesty helps, though the impact still needs to be addressed.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What impact have I missed beyond disappointment?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I stopped making room for plans because I expected them to disappear.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That sounds exhausting and unfair to you.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: It has been exhausting, and I also want to understand your experience.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I have felt pressure to agree before checking what I can manage.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I did not realize agreement felt pressured, and I want to hear more.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: I feared that saying no would be treated as lack of care.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I can see how my reaction may have reinforced that fear.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Can we hold both harms without deciding whose pain is larger?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, comparing pain would distract from whether the pattern can change.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What have we already tried to change this pattern?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We used a shared calendar and agreed to confirm plans the day before.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: The calendar helped briefly, but I stopped updating it consistently.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: And the missing updates brought the same uncertainty back.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Would another tool matter if the habit itself does not change?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Probably not. The change has to be behavioural, not only organizational.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Have there been times when I did follow through well?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, and those weeks felt calmer, but the improvement did not last.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: What made those calmer weeks different?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: You made fewer commitments and told me early when your energy changed.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That suggests a smaller promise might be more honest.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: It might, if the smaller promise still meets enough of both our needs.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: Before we wrap up, can we return to what we said earlier?

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: Yes, I have one more thought about it.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: I am still considering whether we should end the relationship, and I have not chosen an answer tonight.

messages.speaker: other
messages.text: That feels honest.

messages.speaker: self
messages.text: We can continue the discussion soon.
